summary: The magicless-format obligation was introduced. Dictionary setup and the unknown-content-size large-window obligation were already blocked by the same old harness. This timing review covers only the three frozen obligations.

claims.necessity_reason: After the change, streaming decode supports magicless frames when format is set before decoding; the old entry never sets it.

before.requirement: Decode the same valid magicless frame through streaming decompression when supported by the source.
before.reason: The before decoder requires standard frame magic and exposes no magicless streaming format instruction in the supplied contract.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The frame-header parser called by the before stream path rejects a nonstandard prefix.
The before advanced-API heading limits that section to compression.

after.requirement: Set ZSTD_f_zstd1_magicless before streaming decode of a valid magicless frame.
after.reason: The after decoder has a format-aware path, but the old entry initializes the default format and has no call that changes it.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Decoder-context initialization sets the default standard-frame format.
The format-aware parser accepts a missing magic number only when instructed to use the magicless format.

claims.comparison_reason: The same frame and old entry are assessed on both sides. Magicless streaming decode becomes supported after the change; the entry’s absent format-setting call then blocks it.

claims.necessity_reason: Both versions support dictionary initialization for streaming decode, while the fixed entry initializes without a dictionary.

before.requirement: Initialize streaming decompression with a valid matching dictionary before decoding a dictionary-dependent frame.
before.reason: The before source supports dictionary initialization and rejects a frame whose nonzero dictionary ID does not match the decoder context; the entry supplies no dictionary.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The before frame-header check rejects a nonzero dictionary ID absent from the context.
The before dictionary loader establishes the context dictionary ID and entropy state.

after.requirement: Initialize streaming decompression with a valid matching dictionary before decoding a dictionary-dependent frame.
after.reason: The supported dictionary route and dictionary-ID check remain; the old entry still supplies no dictionary or DDict.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The after frame-header check still rejects a mismatched nonzero dictionary ID.
The after dictionary loader still establishes dictionary ID and entropy state.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: This call site shows the entry initializes its stream without dictionary arguments before streaming decode.

claims.comparison_reason: The same dictionary-dependent frame requires matching dictionary setup in both versions. The fixed entry’s no-dictionary initialization is the same blocker.

claims.necessity_reason: Both versions permit a larger maximum-window setting and reject an unknown-content-size frame above the default limit when the old entry omits that setting.

before.requirement: Set a maximum window above the declared window before streaming decode of a valid unknown-content-size frame above the default limit.
before.reason: The before parser accepts a window above 2^27, but unknown content size cannot use the single-pass shortcut; the buffered route checks the unchanged default limit. The entry never calls the available setter.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The before stream decoder applies the maximum-window setting from the primary setter contract and rejects frames above that limit.
Before-version context initialization installs the default maximum-window limit.
The before frame parser permits an unknown content size and a separately declared larger window.
The before header states the 2^27 default and the need to raise the decompression limit for larger windows.

after.requirement: Set a maximum window above the declared window before streaming decode of a valid unknown-content-size frame above the default limit.
after.reason: The after decoder retains the same shortcut guard and window rejection. The old setter remains available alongside the new setter, but the fixed entry calls neither.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The after stream decoder applies the maximum-window setting from the primary setter contract and rejects frames above that limit.
After-version context initialization retains the default maximum-window limit.
The after frame parser permits the same unknown-content-size, larger-window condition.
The newly added setter is an additional way to raise the limit, but the entry does not call it.

claims.comparison_reason: The tuple stays restricted to unknown content size, so neither version’s known-size shortcut is equivalent. Both reject it because the old entry leaves the maximum-window setting at its default.
